- Model consistently overestimates prices, especially in the early part of the forecast horizon (first 5–10 days).
- Forecasts tend to peak too early and then drop too sharply, missing sustained upward momentum.
- Model underestimates late-period price spikes (e.g., 25–30 day horizon) — fails to capture tail risk or policy-driven surges.
- Mean reversion is overemphasized — model too quickly returns to prior levels after spikes, ignoring persistent trends.
- Overshoot after sharp price increases — model reacts too aggressively to recent highs, leading to overcorrection.
- Horizon-specific bias: 30-day forecasts are systematically too high, especially when recent history shows strong upward momentum.
- Model fails to adjust for policy or market sentiment shifts — e.g., ignores regulatory tightening or supply disruptions in the forecast window.
